acts_1.motif: The Ascended Lord & The Cloud of Glory
acts_1.summary: Christ's bodily ascension into the Shekinah cloud of glory fulfills Daniel's vision of the Son of Man approaching the Ancient of Days to receive everlasting dominion and commission His witnesses to the ends of the earth.

nodes.event: Enoch taken up to God; Jacob's ladder connecting heaven and earth
nodes.significance: The primordial archetype of humanity entering the heavenly realm.

nodes.event: The Glory Cloud over the Tabernacle; Elijah taken up into heaven in a chariot of fire
nodes.significance: The divine presence and prophetic ascension anticipating the Lord's return to His throne.

nodes.event: The Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven; 'You ascended on high, leading a host of captives'
nodes.significance: The Messianic ascension to receive universal kingship and bestow gifts upon humanity.

nodes.event: Jesus blesses His disciples as He is parted from them and carried up into heaven
nodes.significance: The historical departure of the risen Christ to be seated at the right hand of the Father.

nodes.event: A cloud takes Jesus out of their sight; 'He who descended is the one who also ascended far above all the heavens'
nodes.significance: The ascended Christ fills all things and equips His Church with spiritual gifts.

nodes.event: 'Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him'; witnesses ascend in a cloud
nodes.significance: The return of the King in the same manner as He ascended, in celestial glory.

acts_1.motif: The Apostolic Twelve & The Restored Tribes
acts_1.summary: The reconstitution of the Twelve Apostles following the apostasy of Judas demonstrates the divine restoration of the twelve tribes of Israel as the foundational pillars of the New Covenant people of God.

nodes.event: The twelve sons of Jacob blessed as patriarchs of the twelve tribes
nodes.significance: The covenant structure of God's chosen family established.

nodes.event: Moses builds twelve pillars at Sinai; Joshua sets up twelve stones from the Jordan
nodes.significance: Memorial stones signifying covenant unity and deliverance across the water.

nodes.event: The holy city with twelve gates named after the twelve tribes of Israel
nodes.significance: Prophecy of the eschatological city of God anchored in the twelvefold covenant people.

nodes.event: Jesus appoints twelve disciples to sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel
nodes.significance: Christ constitutes the Twelve as the core leadership of the Messianic kingdom.

nodes.event: Matthias chosen by lot and prayer to complete the Twelve; peace upon the Israel of God
nodes.significance: The apostolic foundation finalized before the descent of the Holy Spirit.

nodes.event: The wall of the New Jerusalem has twelve foundations, and on them the twelve names of the twelve apostles
nodes.significance: The eternal integration of the Old and New Covenant people in the city of God.

acts_2.summary: The Jewish Feast of Weeks (Shavuot), commemorating the firstfruits and the giving of the Law at Sinai, is fulfilled as the Holy Spirit descends with rushing wind and fire, reversing Babel and writing God's law on human hearts.

nodes.event: The Tower of Babel: Pride scatters humanity into confused languages
nodes.significance: The division of nations and curse of linguistic fragmentation.

nodes.event: Sinai shakes with fire, smoke, and thunder; Feast of Weeks (Pentecost) instituted
nodes.significance: The giving of the law on stone tablets fifty days after Passover.

nodes.event: 'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh'; 'I will put my law within them and write it on their hearts'
nodes.significance: Prophets announce an inner effusion of the divine Spirit across all generations.

nodes.event: John the Baptist prophesies: 'He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire'; rivers of living water
nodes.significance: Jesus promises the indwelling Spirit as the gift of His resurrection and ascension.

nodes.event: Divided tongues of fire rest on each; all hear the mighty works of God in their own tongues
nodes.significance: The curse of Babel reversed; the global Church born as one spiritual body.

nodes.event: Ransomed for God people from every tribe, language, people, and nation before the throne
nodes.significance: The multiracial, multilingual choir of the redeemed singing before the Lamb.

acts_2.motif: The Oath to David & The Holy One Undecayed
acts_2.summary: Peter's Pentecost sermon establishes that David's tomb remains, but God's sworn oath to seat his descendant upon an eternal throne is fulfilled in the resurrection and exaltation of Jesus of Nazareth.

nodes.event: God swears by Himself to bless David and Abraham's seed
nodes.significance: The unconditional divine oath securing redemption.

nodes.event: 'You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor let your Holy One see corruption'
nodes.significance: David prophetically singing of bodily resurrection for the Messianic King.

nodes.event: 'The sure mercies of David'; David my servant shall be their prince forever
nodes.significance: The eternal duration of the Davidic covenant.

nodes.event: 'He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High'; 'He is not here, for He has risen'
nodes.significance: The empty tomb validates Jesus as the immortal King.

nodes.event: 'Being therefore a prophet... he foresaw and spoke of the resurrection of the Christ'
nodes.significance: Apostolic proof of Jesus' resurrection as the true coronation of the Son of David.

nodes.event: 'The words of the holy one, the true one, who has the key of David'
nodes.significance: The permanently enthroned Davidic King opening the gates of the eternal kingdom.

acts_3.motif: The Lame Man Healed & The Times of Refreshing
acts_3.summary: Peter healing the lame beggar at the Beautiful Gate fulfills the Messianic promise that the lame will leap like a deer, pointing forward to the cosmic restoration of all things spoken by the holy prophets.

nodes.event: The ground cursed, bringing pain, weakness, and physical decay
nodes.significance: The entrance of physical infirmity and sorrow into creation.

nodes.event: David shows covenant kindness (hesed) to Mephibosheth, lame in both feet, eating at the king's table
nodes.significance: Grace extended to the crippled in the royal presence of David.

nodes.event: 'Then shall the lame man leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute sing for joy'
nodes.significance: Physical healing as the hallmark of the Messianic kingdom age.

nodes.event: Jesus tells John's disciples: 'The blind see, the lame walk'; healing at the Pool of Bethesda
nodes.significance: Jesus demonstrates His divine identity through authoritative healing of the lame.

nodes.event: 'In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!'; leaping and praising God; times of refreshing
nodes.significance: The name of Jesus exercises continuing resurrection power in the apostolic Church.

nodes.event: No more death, neither sorrow nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain; leaves for healing
nodes.significance: The final, total restoration of creation from all disability and suffering.

acts_4.motif: The Rejected Stone Made the Chief Cornerstone
acts_4.summary: Before the threatening Sanhedrin, Peter proclaims Psalm 118: the Stone rejected by the builders has become the foundational Cornerstone of God's new temple, outside of whose name there is no salvation.

nodes.event: Jacob sets up the stone as a pillar at Bethel; 'The Shepherd, the Stone of Israel'
nodes.significance: The stone of God's presence and covenant foundation.

nodes.event: 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this is the Lord's doing'
nodes.significance: Prophetic song of the builder's rejected stone elevated to primary honor.

nodes.event: 'Behold, I am laying in Zion a foundation stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone'; uncut stone breaks kingdoms
nodes.significance: The divine foundation against which all human hypocrisy falls.

nodes.event: Jesus confronts the chief priests with Psalm 118: 'Have you never read in the Scriptures?'
nodes.significance: Jesus applies the rejected stone directly to His impending rejection by Israel's rulers.

nodes.event: 'This Jesus is the stone that was rejected by you... and there is salvation in no one else'; built on the apostles and prophets
nodes.significance: The cornerstone doctrine of exclusive salvation and the Church as living spiritual temple.

nodes.event: The foundations of the wall of the city adorned with every kind of jewel, bearing the names of the apostles
nodes.significance: The indestructible celestial temple resting upon the eternal cornerstone.

acts_5.motif: The Holy Sanctuary & The Unstoppable Counsel of God
acts_5.summary: The swift judgment upon Ananias and Sapphira for lying to the Holy Spirit demonstrates the fearful holiness of God's new living temple, while Gamaliel unwittingly confesses that work born of God cannot be overthrown.

nodes.event: Cain brings deceptive sacrifice; God warns that sin is crouching at the door
nodes.significance: Hypocrisy and deceit exposed before the all-seeing eyes of God.

nodes.event: Nadab and Abihu offer strange fire; Achan takes devoted things at Jericho
nodes.significance: Immediate divine judgment when holiness is compromised at the inauguration of a covenant era.

nodes.event: 'Take counsel together, but it will come to nothing; for God is with us (Immanuel)'
nodes.significance: The sovereign decree of God standing firm against all human schemes.

nodes.event: 'The gates of hell shall not prevail against it'; 'Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy'
nodes.significance: Christ guarantees the Church's survival while commanding radical sincerity.

nodes.event: 'You have not lied to man but to God'; Gamaliel: 'If it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them'
nodes.significance: The Holy Spirit affirmed as fully personal and divine, purifying and defending the Church.

nodes.event: Nothing unclean shall enter the city, nor anyone who practices abominations or falsehood
nodes.significance: The absolute purity of the final sanctuary where all hypocrisy is eradicated.

acts_6.motif: The Seven Servants & The Unhindered Word
acts_6.summary: The appointment of the Seven Spirit-filled men to care for Hellenistic widows reflects Christ's servant ministry, preserving the apostles for prayer and the ministry of the Word so that the gospel multiplies mightily.

nodes.event: Joseph identified as 'a man in whom is the Spirit of God' to oversee grain distribution
nodes.significance: Wise, Spirit-filled administration preserving the lives of the needy.

nodes.event: Jethro advises Moses to choose able, God-fearing men; seventy elders endowed with the Spirit
nodes.significance: Shared leadership and diaconal burden-bearing in the wilderness assembly.

nodes.event: 'Share your bread with the hungry and bring the homeless poor into your house'
nodes.significance: True covenant fasting and worship expressed in compassionate justice.

nodes.event: Jesus washes disciples' feet; 'The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve'
nodes.significance: Christ establishes servanthood as the supreme qualification for spiritual leadership.

nodes.event: Seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and wisdom, appointed; the Word of God spread
nodes.significance: Diaconal care established as an integral ministry protecting gospel advance.

nodes.event: They serve Him day and night in His temple, and He will shelter them; the Lamb will be their Shepherd
nodes.significance: Eternal service of the saints before the throne in unhindered fellowship.

acts_8.motif: The Ethiopian Eunuch & The Suffering Servant
acts_8.summary: Philip explains Isaiah 53 to Candace's court official: the outcast foreigner excluded by the Mosaic law is immersed in water and incorporated into the covenant family through the humiliation of the Lamb.

nodes.event: Blessing to all families of earth; 'Cush (Ethiopia) shall stretch out her hands to God'
nodes.significance: The ancient promise of African and distant Gentile inclusion in the kingdom.

nodes.event: Eunuchs excluded from entering the assembly of the Lord under Mosaic ceremonial boundaries
nodes.significance: The physical barrier of the Old Covenant highlighting human defect and exclusion.

nodes.event: Like a sheep led to slaughter; 'Let not the eunuch say: Behold, I am a dry tree... I will give them an everlasting name'
nodes.significance: Prophecy that the Messiah's suffering would open covenant adoption to eunuchs.

nodes.event: Jesus honors eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom; the poor have good news preached to them
nodes.significance: Christ breaks through ceremonial ostracism to welcome outcasts.

nodes.event: Philip preaches Jesus from Isaiah 53; the eunuch baptized: 'See, here is water! What hinders me?'
nodes.significance: Immediate, radical inclusion of the Ethiopian eunuch into the body of Christ.

nodes.event: People from every tribe, language, people, and nation made a kingdom and priests to our God
nodes.significance: The worldwide gathering of all formerly excluded peoples singing before the Lamb.

acts_9.motif: The Damascus Road & The Transformed Persecutor
acts_9.summary: The blinding celestial light unhorses Saul of Tarsus as Christ reveals His mystical union with the Church ('Why do you persecute Me?'), converting the fiercest enemy of the cross into the chosen vessel to the Gentiles.

nodes.event: Jacob wrestles with God at Peniel; stricken on the hip and given a new name, Israel
nodes.significance: The proud patriarch humbled by divine encounter to become a vessel of blessing.

nodes.event: Moses hidden in the cleft of the rock; Saul falls under the prophetic spirit
nodes.significance: The devastating and blinding majesty of the divine presence.

nodes.event: A light to the nations; Ezekiel falls on his face before the radiant likeness of the glory of the Lord
nodes.significance: Prophetic commissioning accompanied by overwhelming heavenly brilliance.

nodes.event: 'As you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to Me'
nodes.significance: Christ teaches that persecution of His disciples is persecution of Himself.

nodes.event: 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting; he is a chosen instrument of mine to carry my name to Gentiles'
nodes.significance: The chief of sinners transformed by sovereign grace into the apostle of grace.

nodes.event: His face was like the sun shining in full strength; John falls at His feet as though dead
nodes.significance: The sovereign glory of the risen Lord conquering and illuminating the nations.

acts_10.motif: The Clean Sheet & The Ingathering of the Gentiles
acts_10.summary: Peter's vision on the Joppa rooftop of a great sheet descending with clean and unclean beasts destroys the ceremonial dividing wall, proving that what God has cleansed through Christ's blood no person may call unholy.

nodes.event: Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you; all families blessed in Abraham
nodes.significance: The original post-flood dietary freedom and universal blessing promise.

nodes.event: Distinction between clean and unclean beasts separating holy Israel from surrounding nations
nodes.significance: Pedagogical dietary barriers designed to maintain Israel's ceremonial separation.

nodes.event: Nations shall come to your light; ten men from all languages take hold of a Jew's robe
nodes.significance: The prophetic horizon of Gentile inclusion in the worship of the God of Israel.

nodes.event: Jesus declares all foods clean; 'Many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham'
nodes.significance: Jesus purifies the heart and signals the imminent inclusion of Gentiles.

nodes.event: 'What God has made clean, do not call common'; the Holy Spirit falls on Cornelius' household
nodes.significance: The ceremonial barrier abolished; Gentile Pentecost confirming equal status in the covenant.

nodes.event: A great multitude from every nation; the nations walk by the light of the Lamb
nodes.significance: The cosmic banquet where all redeemed humanity shares the glory of God.

acts_11.motif: The First Called Christians & The Antioch Fellowship
acts_11.summary: At Antioch the disciples are first called 'Christians' as Jewish and Gentile believers unite in table fellowship and send famine relief to Judea, demonstrating that Christ's blood creates a transnational family of sacrificial love.

nodes.event: Joseph sends grain and relief to preserve his estranged brothers during widespread famine
nodes.significance: Love and material sustenance across geographical separation.

nodes.event: 'Open wide your hand to your brother'; 'Behold how good and pleasant it is when brothers dwell in unity'
nodes.significance: The covenant requirement of mutual aid and fraternal unity.

nodes.event: 'The nations shall see your righteousness... and you shall be called by a new name'
nodes.significance: Prophecy of the new covenant name given by the mouth of the Lord.

nodes.event: 'By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another'
nodes.significance: Mutual sacrificial love established as the unmistakable badge of discipleship.

nodes.event: Disciples first called Christians in Antioch; sending relief according to ability to brothers in Judea
nodes.significance: The new covenant identity realized in multi-ethnic unity and practical generosity.

nodes.event: I will write on him the name of my God and my own new name
nodes.significance: The permanent inscription of Christ's name upon all who overcome.

acts_12.motif: The Angel of Deliverance & The Smitten Tyrant
acts_12.summary: Peter's midnight release from chained Herod Agrippa's prison through angelic intervention contrasts with the tyrant Herod accepting divine praise and being struck dead by God, proving the Word of God cannot be chained.

nodes.event: Angels lay hold of Lot's hand to rescue him from doomed Sodom
nodes.significance: Angelic deliverance pulling God's people out of immediate peril.

nodes.event: Death of Egypt's firstborn and Herod's counterpart Pharaoh; God sends His angel to shut lions' mouths
nodes.significance: Judgment upon persecuting monarchs and miraculous preservation of God's servants.

nodes.event: 'I will ascend above the heights; but you are brought down to Sheol'; judgment on Tyre: 'You say, I am a god'
nodes.significance: Prophetic condemnation of proud rulers usurping divine honors.

nodes.event: Gates of hell shall not prevail; 'He has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts, and brought down the mighty'
nodes.significance: Jesus and Mary proclaim the overthrow of worldly tyrants by divine sovereignty.

nodes.event: Chains fall off Peter; Herod eaten by worms; 'But the word of God increased and multiplied'
nodes.significance: The unstoppable advance of the gospel over the corpses of its persecutors.

nodes.event: Fallen is Babylon the great; the beast and false prophet thrown into the lake of fire
nodes.significance: The final, decisive execution of divine judgment against all anti-Christian empires.

acts_13.motif: The Sure Mercies of David & The Light of the Gentiles
acts_13.summary: In the synagogue of Pisidian Antioch, Paul preaches the core apostolic kerygma: Christ's resurrection fulfills the Davidic covenant and Psalm 16 ('You will not allow your Holy One to see corruption'), sending the gospel to the ends of the earth.

nodes.event: The Abrahamic promise that in the Seed all nations shall be blessed
nodes.significance: The baseline covenant oath Paul cites in his missionary preaching.

nodes.event: 'For you will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor let your Holy One see corruption'
nodes.significance: Davidic Psalm predicting that the royal Messiah will escape bodily decay.

nodes.event: 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David'; 'I will make you as a light for the nations'
nodes.significance: Prophecy that the Davidic covenant blessings will flow outward to enlighten the Gentiles.

nodes.event: Simeon: 'A light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to your people Israel'; Great Commission
nodes.significance: Jesus recognized as the personal light to the nations.

nodes.event: 'David saw corruption, but He whom God raised did not'; 'I have made you a light for the Gentiles'
nodes.significance: Justification by faith in the resurrected Christ offered to both Jews and Gentiles.

nodes.event: The glory of God gives it light, and its lamp is the Lamb; the nations walk by its light
nodes.significance: The eternal illumination of the redeemed world by the risen Davidic King.

acts_14.motif: The Living Creator & The Door of Faith
acts_14.summary: At Lystra, Paul turns pagans from worshiping Zeus and Hermes to the living God who provides rain and fruitful seasons, enduring near-fatal stoning to confirm that through many tribulations we must enter the Kingdom of God.

nodes.event: 'While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter shall not cease'
nodes.significance: The Noahic covenant of common grace and providential order.

nodes.event: Prohibition of idols; 'Our God is in the heavens; idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands'
nodes.significance: The radical distinction between the living God and inert pagan idols.

nodes.event: 'The Lord is the true God; He is the living God and the everlasting King; can any of the false gods of the nations bring rain?'
nodes.significance: Prophetic satire against pagan mythology and idolatry.

nodes.event: The Father makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good; 'In the world you will have tribulation; be of good cheer'
nodes.significance: Christ teaches divine common grace alongside the necessity of cross-bearing.

nodes.event: 'Turn from these vain things to a living God'; 'Through many tribulations we enter the kingdom'; opened a door of faith to Gentiles
nodes.significance: Apostolic evangelism to pagans based on creation, providence, and persevering faith.

nodes.event: 'Worship Him who made heaven and earth, the sea and the springs of water'; 'These are the ones coming out of the great tribulation'
nodes.significance: Cosmic adoration of the Creator by those who overcame tribulation through faith.

acts_15.motif: The Rebuilt Tent of David & Salvation by Grace
acts_15.summary: The Jerusalem Council rules that Gentiles are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus without Mosaic circumcision, citing Amos 9: God rebuilds the fallen booth of David so that the remnant of mankind may seek the Lord.

nodes.event: Circumcision instituted after Abraham was already justified by faith
nodes.significance: The chronological priority of faith over the ceremonial sign.

nodes.event: Loving the stranger as oneself; the eternal booth and dynasty of David
nodes.significance: The inclusion of foreigners and the permanence of David's house.

nodes.event: 'In that day I will raise up the booth of David that is fallen... that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations'
nodes.significance: The explicit prophetic promise that the restored Davidic kingdom embraces Gentiles.

nodes.event: 'My yoke is easy, and my burden is light'; 'If the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed'
nodes.significance: Jesus removes the crushing yoke of legalistic self-justification.

nodes.event: 'We believe that we will be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they will'; James cites Amos 9
nodes.significance: The definitive apostolic declaration that salvation is by grace alone through faith alone.

nodes.event: 'You ransomed people for God from every tribe and language'; God's dwelling tent is with man
nodes.significance: The fully rebuilt and glorified tent of David filled with saints from all nations.

acts_16.motif: Midnight Hymns in Prison & The Roman Jailer
acts_16.summary: Paul and Silas singing praises with bleeding backs in the Philippian dungeon followed by a midnight earthquake shatters imperial prison chains, bringing the despairing Roman jailer and his household to joyful baptism.

nodes.event: Joseph imprisoned in Egypt, yet the Lord was with him and showed him steadfast love
nodes.significance: The faithful servant praising God in unjust incarceration.

nodes.event: 'By night His song is with me'; 'He brought them out of darkness and broke their chains in pieces'
nodes.significance: Songs in the night and divine liberation from literal iron shackles.

nodes.event: To bring out the prisoners from the dungeon; proclaiming liberty to the captives
nodes.significance: Messianic mission to dismantle physical and spiritual prisons.

nodes.event: Jesus sings a hymn with His disciples before Gethsemane; the dying thief saved at the brink of death
nodes.significance: Praise amidst impending suffering and salvation granted at the point of despair.

nodes.event: Paul and Silas praying and singing hymns at midnight; 'Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household'
nodes.significance: The irresistible power of worship and gospel proclamation to turn pagan households into churches.

nodes.event: Christ holds the keys of Death and Hades; the great multitude sings Hallelujah in celestial triumph
nodes.significance: The ultimate shattering of death's dungeon by the risen Lord.

acts_17.motif: The Unknown God & The Resurrected Judge
acts_17.summary: On the Areopagus in Athens, Paul proclaims the sovereign Creator who does not dwell in temples made with hands, commanding all men everywhere to repent because God has fixed a day of judgment through the Man raised from the dead.

nodes.event: God breathes into man's nostrils the breath of life; one common human origin
nodes.significance: The universal fatherhood of God in creation uniting all races into one blood.

nodes.event: 'Will God indeed dwell on earth? Behold, heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you'; earth is the Lord's
nodes.significance: The absolute transcendence of the Creator over humanly constructed shrines.

nodes.event: 'He who created the heavens... who gives breath to the people on it; heaven is my throne'
nodes.significance: Prophetic rebuke to idolaters attempting to house or feed the uncreated God.

nodes.event: 'God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth'; given authority to execute judgment
nodes.significance: Jesus defines true spiritual worship and claims universal judicial authority.

nodes.event: 'In Him we live and move and have our being'; God has fixed a day on which He will judge the world by the Man He appointed
nodes.significance: Apostolic philosophy confronting pagan polytheism with the historical resurrection.

nodes.event: The earth and sky flee from His face; I saw no temple, for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple
nodes.significance: The final judgment by the resurrected Christ and the unmediated worship of eternity.

acts_18.motif: The Covenant Reassurance: 'I Am with You'
acts_18.summary: Facing intense Jewish opposition in Corinth, the Lord appears to Paul in a night vision with the covenant formula given to Moses, Joshua, and Jeremiah: 'Do not be afraid, for I am with you, and I have many people in this city.'

nodes.event: God appears to Isaac and Jacob: 'Fear not, for I am with you and will bless you'
nodes.significance: The divine pledge of personal accompaniment to the covenant patriarchs.

nodes.event: 'Certainly I will be with you'; 'As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; do not be frightened'
nodes.significance: Divine presence enabling covenant leaders to accomplish impossible tasks.

nodes.event: 'Do not be afraid of their faces, for I am with you to deliver you'; 'Fear not, for I am with you'
nodes.significance: Prophetic fortitude sustained solely by the presence of the Lord.

nodes.event: 'They shall call His name Immanuel (God with us)'; 'Behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age'
nodes.significance: Jesus embodies and fulfills the covenant presence in His own divine person.

nodes.event: The Lord speaks to Paul: 'Do not be afraid, but go on speaking... for I am with you, and no one will harm you'
nodes.significance: The ascended Christ actively sustaining His missionary apostles in hostile metropolitan centers.

nodes.event: 'Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man. He will dwell with them, and they will be His people'
nodes.significance: The eternal, unbroken presence of God with His redeemed community forever.

acts_19.motif: The Overthrow of Idols & The Prevailing Word
acts_19.summary: In Ephesus, the center of magic and the imperial cult of Artemis, the name of Jesus is magnified as converts burn their occult books worth 50,000 drachmas, proving that the Word of the Lord grows mightily and prevails over demonic empires.

nodes.event: Jacob commands his household: 'Put away the foreign gods that are among you and purify yourselves'
nodes.significance: The renunciation of domestic idols and occult charms before entering Bethel.

nodes.event: Judgment against all the gods of Egypt; Dagon falls face down and broken before the Ark of the Lord
nodes.significance: God demonstrates total supremacy over pagan deities and talismans.

nodes.event: 'The idols shall utterly pass away; in that day mankind will cast away their idols of silver and gold'
nodes.significance: Prophecy of the voluntary destruction of pagan cultic images.

nodes.event: 'If it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you'
nodes.significance: Jesus binds the strong man (Satan) and plunders his house.

nodes.event: Many burned their books of magic arts openly; 'So the word of the Lord continued to increase and prevail mightily'
nodes.significance: The gospel breaking the occult and financial stronghold of idolatry in the ancient world.

nodes.event: The merchants of the earth weep over fallen Babylon; sorcerers cast into the lake of fire
nodes.significance: The final, permanent overthrow of all commercial idolatry, witchcraft, and deception.

acts_20.motif: The Flock Purchased with God's Own Blood
acts_20.summary: Paul's tearful farewell to the Ephesian elders at Miletus emphasizes the sacrificial pastoral care of Christ the Chief Shepherd, charging the elders to guard the flock of God which He purchased with His own divine blood.

nodes.event: Jacob blesses Joseph: 'The God who has been my Shepherd all my life long to this day'
nodes.significance: Patriarchal recognition of God as the tender, lifelong Shepherd of His people.

nodes.event: 'The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want'; David chosen to shepherd Jacob His people with integrity
nodes.significance: The Davidic archetype combining royal rule with sacrificial shepherd care.

nodes.event: 'I myself will search for my sheep and seek them out'; 'Awake, O sword, against my Shepherd, against the man who stands next to me'
nodes.significance: Prophecy of God Himself shepherding Israel through the smitten Shepherd-Companion.

nodes.event: 'I am the Good Shepherd; the Good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep'
nodes.significance: Jesus claims the divine shepherd identity and offers His life as the ransom.

nodes.event: 'Pay careful attention to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to care for the church of God, which He obtained with His own blood'
nodes.significance: The profound theological affirmation of Christ's blood as God's own blood purchasing the Church.

nodes.event: 'For the Lamb in the midst of the throne will be their Shepherd, and He will guide them to springs of living water'
nodes.significance: The eternal paradox: the slain Lamb reigns forever as the caring Shepherd of His people.

acts_21.motif: Paul's Bound Hands & The Way of the Cross
acts_21.summary: Agabus binding his hands with Paul's belt prefigures the apostle willingly entering Jerusalem to be delivered into the hands of the Gentiles, deliberately walking in the footsteps of Christ toward the cross.

nodes.event: Isaac bound by his father Abraham and laid upon the wood of the altar
nodes.significance: The willing submission of the beloved son to be bound for sacrifice.

nodes.event: 'Bind the festal sacrifice with cords, up to the horns of the altar'; David ascends the Mount of Olives weeping
nodes.significance: The sacrificial victim bound; the righteous king suffering rejection.

nodes.event: Prophets using symbolic physical signs (yokes, linen belts, lying on side) to dramatize divine decrees
nodes.significance: The prophetic tradition of acted parables depicting covenant bondage and deliverance.

nodes.event: 'The Son of Man will be delivered over to the Gentiles to be mocked and crucified'; Peter told: 'Another will gird you and carry you where you do not wish to go'
nodes.significance: Jesus willingly goes up to Jerusalem and foretells the martyrdom of His servants.

nodes.event: Agabus binds hands: 'So will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man who owns this belt'; 'I am ready not only to be bound but to die for the name of the Lord Jesus'
nodes.significance: Paul's radical conformity to the sufferings of Christ for the sake of His body, the Church.

nodes.event: 'They loved not their lives even unto death'; 'These are they who follow the Lamb wherever He goes'
nodes.significance: The martyr church crowned in glory for following the footsteps of the Lamb.

acts_22.motif: The Heavenly Commission & The Light of the Gentiles
acts_22.summary: Speaking in Hebrew on the temple stairs, Paul recounts his encounter with the blazing celestial light of Jesus of Nazareth, climaxing in the explosive divine commission that shattered ethnocentric nationalism: 'Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles.'

nodes.event: God calls Abraham out of his homeland: 'In you all the families of the earth shall be blessed'
nodes.significance: The original missionary commission to leave ancestral comfort for the nations.

nodes.event: Moses called at the burning bush; Solomon prays that foreigners may know and fear the name of the Lord
nodes.significance: The divine sending of deliverers and the open invitation for nations to know God.

nodes.event: 'Here am I! Send me'; 'It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob; I will make you a light to the nations'
nodes.significance: The prophetic commissioning to carry salvation to the ends of the earth.

nodes.event: Simeon: 'A light for revelation to the Gentiles'; 'Go therefore and make disciples of all nations'
nodes.significance: Christ defines the universal scope of the New Covenant mission.

nodes.event: 'You will be a witness for Him to everyone... Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles'
nodes.significance: Paul's specialized apostolic vocation as the chosen vessel to the Gentile world.

nodes.event: The nations shall walk by the light of the Lamb, and the kings of the earth bring their glory into it
nodes.significance: The ultimate fulfillment of the Gentile mission in the New Jerusalem.

acts_23.motif: The Sanhedrin Divided & The Unshakable Decree
acts_23.summary: When the Sanhedrin erupts over the hope of the resurrection, the risen Lord stands beside Paul in the Roman barracks at night with the unbreakable decree: 'Take courage, for as you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so you must also bear witness in Rome.'

nodes.event: The Lord appears in a night vision: 'Fear not, Abram, I am your shield'; 'I will go down with you to Egypt'
nodes.significance: Covenant nocturnal revelations providing divine security and purpose.

nodes.event: Why do the nations conspire? He who sits in the heavens laughs; 'The Lord is on my side; I will not fear'
nodes.significance: The futility of human conspiracies against the Lord's anointed.

nodes.event: 'No weapon that is fashioned against you shall succeed'; 'They will fight against you, but they shall not prevail against you'
nodes.significance: Prophetic guarantee of divine invincibility until one's assigned task is finished.

nodes.event: 'Do not be anxious how you are to speak... for the Spirit of your Father will speak through you'; 'Take heart; I have overcome the world'
nodes.significance: Christ promises inward courage and heavenly advocacy before hostile tribunals.

nodes.event: The Lord stood by him and said: 'Take courage... you must also bear witness in Rome'; 'The Lord stood by me and strengthened me'
nodes.significance: The sovereign presence of Christ guaranteeing that no conspiracy of forty men can thwart Rome's destiny.

nodes.event: 'Behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut'
nodes.significance: The absolute sovereignty of the King who opens doors that no adversary can close.

acts_24.motif: Righteousness, Self-Control, & The Judgment to Come
acts_24.summary: Before Governor Felix and Drusilla, Paul refuses political flattery and reasons concerning righteousness, self-control, and coming judgment, causing the corrupt Roman ruler to tremble before the moral authority of Christ.

nodes.event: Abraham intercedes: 'Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is right and just?'
nodes.significance: The foundational moral standard of God's universal judicial righteousness.

nodes.event: 'You shall not pervert justice... and you shall take no bribe'; 'When one rules justly over men, ruling in the fear of God'
nodes.significance: The divine demand for incorruptible integrity in human magistrate office.

nodes.event: 'Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream'; to do justice and love kindness
nodes.significance: Prophetic denunciation of tyrannical corruption and exploitation.

nodes.event: The Holy Spirit convicts the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment; the Son of Man separates nations
nodes.significance: The threefold conviction of the Holy Spirit proclaimed before the world.

nodes.event: Paul reasons of righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, and Felix was terrified; striving to have a clear conscience
nodes.significance: The prophetic witness of the gospel convicting worldly rulers of their eternal accountability.

nodes.event: Kings of the earth hide from the wrath of the Lamb; the dead judged according to what was written in the books
nodes.significance: The impartial, unavoidable judgment seat before which all rulers must stand.

acts_25.motif: The Appeal to Caesar & The Providential Hand
acts_25.summary: Confronting judicial bribery and Jewish ambush, Paul invokes his Roman citizenship with the fateful words 'I appeal to Caesar,' using imperial legal structures to fulfill the sovereign divine decree that he must preach in the capital of the world.

nodes.event: Joseph tells his brothers: 'As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring it about that many people should be kept alive'
nodes.significance: The supreme Old Testament archetype of providence subverting human malice.

nodes.event: 'The king's heart is a stream of water in the hand of the Lord; He turns it wherever He will'; 'Who knows whether you have not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?'
nodes.significance: God using pagan imperial courts and decrees to fulfill covenant preservation.

nodes.event: God names Persian Cyrus His anointed; Nebuchadnezzar as His servant to accomplish historical judgment
nodes.significance: Sovereign deployment of secular empires as instruments in redemptive history.

nodes.event: Jesus tells Pilate: 'You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given you from above'
nodes.significance: Christ recognizes that secular magistrates are bounded by divine permission.

nodes.event: Paul: 'I am standing before Caesar's tribunal, where I ought to be tried... I appeal to Caesar'; Festus: 'To Caesar you shall go'
nodes.significance: Paul's legal strategy leveraging civil rights to advance the kingdom of God.

nodes.event: Jesus Christ, the ruler of kings on earth; the Lamb will conquer them, for He is Lord of lords and King of kings
nodes.significance: The ultimate triumph of the King of Kings over every earthly Caesar and empire.

acts_26.motif: The Defense Before Agrippa & The Hope of the Fathers
acts_26.summary: Before King Agrippa and Bernice in regal splendor, Paul testifies that he stands on trial for nothing other than the foundational hope promised by God to the fathers: that the Messiah must suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, proclaim light to Jews and Gentiles.

nodes.event: The covenant promise made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob of universal blessing
nodes.significance: The 'hope of the promise made by God to our fathers' which anchors Paul's defense.

nodes.event: 'You are my Son; ask of me and I will give you the nations'; 'You will not let your Holy One see corruption'
nodes.significance: The royal and resurrection promises forming the bedrock of Israel's national hope.

nodes.event: The Servant as a light for the nations; after His soul makes an offering for sin, He shall see His offspring and prolong His days
nodes.significance: Moses and the Prophets explicitly foretelling the Messiah's suffering and resurrection.

nodes.event: 'Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer these things and enter into His glory?'; beginning with Moses and all the Prophets
nodes.significance: Jesus defines the gospel as the exact fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy.

nodes.event: 'Why is it thought incredible by any of you that God raises the dead?'; Christ the first to rise from the dead, proclaiming light
nodes.significance: Apostolic apologetic demonstrating that Christianity is the true fulfillment of biblical Judaism.

nodes.event: Jesus Christ the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of kings on earth
nodes.significance: The eternal exaltation of the Firstborn from the dead acknowledged by all earthly kings.

acts_27.motif: The Shipwreck & The Angel of Divine Preservation
acts_27.summary: During the catastrophic fourteen-day Mediterranean tempest Euroclydon, the angel of God assures Paul that not a single life aboard will be lost, prefiguring Christ's unbreakable preservation of His pilgrim Church through the storms of history.

nodes.event: Noah and his household preserved in the Ark through the deluge; 'God remembered Noah'
nodes.significance: The primordial vessel of salvation riding above the chaotic waters of death.

nodes.event: Those who go down to the sea in ships; He calms the storm, and they rejoice at the quiet haven
nodes.significance: The Lord's sovereign mastery over roaring tempestuous seas.

nodes.event: 'When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you'
nodes.significance: The covenant guarantee of preservation through deep waters.

nodes.event: Jesus rebukes the wind and waves on the Sea of Galilee: 'Peace! Be still!'; walking on water to rescue Peter
nodes.significance: Jesus demonstrates divine authority over chaotic waters and panic-stricken disciples.

nodes.event: The angel declares: 'Do not be afraid, Paul; God has granted you all who sail with you'; all 276 souls escape safely to land
nodes.significance: Paul breaks bread and gives thanks in the storm; total preservation of life granted for the apostle's sake.

nodes.event: 'And the sea was no more'; the redeemed standing victorious on the sea of glass mingled with fire
nodes.significance: The chaotic waters of death and judgment eradicated forever in the New Creation.

acts_28.motif: The Viper Shaken Off & The Unhindered Kingdom
acts_28.summary: Paul shakes off the deadly viper into the fire on Malta unharmed, fulfilling Christ's promise of authority over serpents, and arrives in Rome to preach the Kingdom of God and teach about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance.

nodes.event: The seed of the woman crushing the serpent; in your offspring all families of earth blessed
nodes.significance: The initial victory over the serpent and promise of global reach.

nodes.event: 'You will tread on the lion and the adder; the young lion and the serpent you will trample underfoot'
nodes.significance: The righteous granted immunity and triumph over venomous adversaries.

nodes.event: 'The nursing child shall play over the hole of the cobra, and the weaned child put his hand on the adder's den'
nodes.significance: The pacification of the serpent's enmity in the peaceful Messianic kingdom.

nodes.event: 'Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions... and nothing shall hurt you'
nodes.significance: Christ imparts spiritual dominion over demonic toxicity and physical harm to His witnesses.

nodes.event: Paul shakes off the viper into the fire; in Rome, preaching the kingdom of God with all boldness, unhindered (akolytos)
nodes.significance: The triumphant climax of Acts: the gospel breaks out of Judea and takes root unhindered in the capital of the world.

nodes.event: The ancient serpent seized and bound for a thousand years; 'Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!'
